claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have children - I have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Now I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Do you live with Alex, or are you paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. A few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in residential accommodation for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a while now, a few months actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. This is important information as hospital stays can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me more specifically how long Alex has been in hospital - is it more or less than 12 weeks? And do you regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital (for example, on clothes, toys, books, or other items)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been more than 12 weeks - about 15 weeks now. And yes, I still regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital - you know, buying clothes, magazines, their favorite snacks, things like that to make them more comfortable.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have enough details now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation against the rules:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- You are responsible for Alex and they normally live with you ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓
- Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (15 weeks)
- However, you regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital

According to the rules, after 12 weeks in hospital, you would usually no longer be entitled to Child Benefit. **However, there is an important exception**: for children in a UK hospital, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on them - which you are doing.

Based on your circumstances, you should be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** Based on the information you've provided, you are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you qualify under an important exception: Child Benefit can continue for children in UK hospitals if you regularly spend money on them - which you're doing by buying clothes, magazines, snacks, and other items.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you should make a claim. If you're already receiving it, you should continue to be entitled to it as long as you keep regularly spending money on Alex during their hospital stay.

I hope Alex recovers soon!
